name: talaria-code
description: Talaria Code — an in-editor client for the Hermes agent: chat, tools, MCP, skills, checkpoints and more, in a native VS Code panel.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In an untrusted (Restricted Mode) workspace Talaria Code runs only its process-free mock backend: it will not spawn the Hermes agent (`hermes acp` / `python -m tui_gateway.entry`), will not index the codebase (file walk + embeddings upload), and will not bind the read-only LSP-over-HTTP MCP server that exposes live language-server intelligence (diagnostics, definitions, references, symbols, hover) to the agent. Grant Workspace Trust to enable the real backend, RAG indexing, and LSP tools.

virtualWorkspaces.description: In a virtual workspace Talaria Code cannot spawn its local child processes or index a real on-disk codebase; only the mock backend and inline autocomplete are available.

hermes.hermesPath.markdownDescription: Absolute path to the `hermes` executable (e.g. a virtualenv `bin/hermes`). Leave empty to discover it from the login-shell `PATH` (`command -v hermes`). Set this when PATH discovery cannot work — Flatpak VS Code, Remote-SSH with a non-login PATH, or a custom install location. Ignored while `#hermes.backend#` is `mock`. Machine-scoped: a workspace cannot override it (prevents a malicious repo from repointing the executable — security).

hermes.pythonPath.markdownDescription: Absolute path to the Python interpreter used to launch the real Hermes backend (e.g. a virtualenv `bin/python`). Leave empty to resolve `python` from the login-shell `PATH`. Ignored while `#hermes.backend#` is `mock`. Machine-scoped: a workspace cannot override this (prevents a malicious repo from repointing the interpreter — security).

hermes.cwd.markdownDescription: Working directory for the Hermes agent process. Leave empty to use the first workspace folder. Ignored while `#hermes.backend#` is `mock`. Machine-scoped: not workspace-overridable (security).

enumDescriptions: Canned streaming + panel data. Spawns no process; runs on any OS. Default.
Real backend: spawns `hermes acp` over JSON-RPC/stdio (Fedora/Linux). Wired later.
hermes.backend.description: Which agent backend the extension talks to. Machine-scoped: a workspace cannot flip this to `acp` to force a process spawn (security).

hermes.dashboardPort.markdownDescription: Loopback port for the Hermes dashboard REST server (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>`) that powers the real Skills & Tools panels. If a dashboard is already listening there it is adopted; otherwise the extension spawns `python -m hermes_cli.main serve --port <port>` (Fedora/Linux). Ignored while `#hermes.backend#` is `mock`. Machine-scoped: a workspace cannot repoint it (security).

enumDescriptions: Secure default. Never adopts a pre-existing dashboard: always spawns and provenance-verifies its own child before use.

Legacy, INSECURE opt-in: adopts any already-running responder whose /api/status body merely LOOKS like Hermes, with no further verification. Only for coexisting with an already-running Hermes desktop holding the port.
hermes.dashboardAdopt.markdownDescription: How the extension discovers the Hermes dashboard REST server on `#hermes.dashboardPort#`. `spawn-only` (default, secure) never adopts a foreign peer — it always spawns its own child and verifies the healthy server's served session token has the provenance of that spawn before use (CWE-306/346). `shape` is a legacy, INSECURE opt-in that adopts any responder whose `/api/status` body is merely Hermes-shaped, which a local process could spoof; use it only to coexist with an already-running Hermes desktop instance. Ignored while `#hermes.backend#` is `mock`. Machine-scoped: a workspace cannot weaken this (security).

hermes.autocomplete.backend.markdownDescription: Which FIM backend serves autocomplete requests. Machine-scoped: a workspace cannot flip this to a cloud backend and redirect your code off the machine (security — this setting SELECTS the endpoint).

hermes.autocomplete.endpoint.markdownDescription: Base URL for the autocomplete backend (may be a remote node). Leave empty to use the backend's default (Ollama `http://127.0.0.1:11434`, llama.cpp `http://127.0.0.1:8080`, vLLM `http://127.0.0.1:8000`). Machine-scoped: a workspace cannot redirect where your code context is sent (security).

hermes.autocomplete.model.description: Model name/id used for FIM completions. Machine-scoped: a workspace cannot silently repoint completions at a different model (security).

hermes.autocomplete.debounceMs.description: Debounce delay (ms) before triggering a completion request.

hermes.autocomplete.maxPromptTokens.description: Token budget for the assembled prefix/suffix prompt.

hermes.autocomplete.apiKey.markdownDescription: **Deprecated — use the `Talaria: Set Autocomplete API Key` command instead**, which stores the key in the OS keychain (SecretStorage). API key for backends that require auth (e.g. `codestral`, `openai-compat`). A value here is migrated into SecretStorage on activation and then cleared. Machine-scoped: not workspace-overridable (security).

hermes.autocomplete.crossFile.enabled.description: Gather cross-file context (recently-edited and recently-opened files) for autocomplete, when the configured backend/model support a cross-file channel. Has no effect when the backend/model expose none (falls back to single-file completion).

hermes.autocomplete.crossFile.prefixInje.markdownDescription: Inject cross-file snippets as comments into the prompt for backends with no native cross-file channel (Ollama, Codestral, openai-compat). **Loopback-gated by default**: only takes effect when `#hermes.autocomplete.endpoint#` resolves to a loopback host (127.0.0.1/localhost), unless `#hermes.autocomplete.crossFile.prefixInjectionRemote#` is also enabled — so turning this on for a local Ollama does not silently start sending workspace snippets to a remote endpoint. A low-signal channel; default-off.

**Security-sensitive.** Allows `#hermes.autocomplete.crossFile.prefixInjection#` to take effect for a REMOTE (non-loopback) `#hermes.autocomplete.endpoint#` too, sending workspace code snippets from OTHER files to that endpoint (not just the active file's prefix/suffix, which is already sent). Leave off unless you trust the configured remote endpoint with your workspace's code. Machine-scoped: a workspace cannot enable this on its own (security).

hermes.autocomplete.crossFile.warmUp.markdownDescription: Experimental: fire a llama.cpp KV-cache warm-up request (`/infill` with an empty prompt, snippets only) whenever the cross-file snippet set regenerates, so the next real completion hits a warm cache. Only takes effect with the `llamacpp` backend (other backends ignore this setting) and still honors the same untrusted-remote/enabled guards as regular completions. Default-off; a latency optimization, not required for cross-file completions to work.

hermes.rag.enabled.description: Enable the codebase RAG indexer and MCP search server.

hermes.rag.embedEndpoint.description: Base URL for the embeddings backend (Ollama/llama.cpp/vLLM-compatible; may be a remote node). Machine-scoped: a workspace cannot redirect where whole-file embeddings are sent (security).

hermes.rag.embedModel.description: Model name/id used to embed code chunks. Machine-scoped: a workspace cannot silently repoint embeddings at a different model (integrity — same rationale as hermes.autocomplete.model).

hermes.rag.dims.markdownDescription: Matryoshka truncation width for embeddings, forwarded as the OpenAI `dimensions` field. **`0` (default) means: do not send the field at all and let the server decide.** Only set a positive value if your model and runner support it — llama.cpp ignores the field, Ollama truncates, and vLLM answers HTTP 400 for a non-Matryoshka model, which fails the whole index build. Changing this value changes the index fingerprint and forces a full rebuild.

hermes.rag.maxChunkTokens.description: Approximate max tokens per indexed chunk.

hermes.rag.indexDir.description: Workspace-relative directory where the vector index is stored. Machine-scoped: not workspace-overridable (security).

hermes.rag.excludeGlobs.description: Extra glob patterns to exclude from indexing, beyond .gitignore/.hermesignore.

hermes.lib.enabled.markdownDescription: Expose the editor's live language-server intelligence (diagnostics, definitions, references, symbols, hover) to the Hermes agent as read-only MCP tools over an authenticated loopback server. Read-only; requires a trusted workspace (ignored in Restricted Mode). Machine-scoped: a workspace cannot enable it (security).

id.description: Stable identifier for this mode (used on the wire and to match it up when re-selected).

name.description: Display name shown in the mode picker.

deny.description: Rules the agent may NOT edit: an exact workspace-relative path, a directory prefix ending '/', or a basename suffix '*.ext'.

allowOnly.description: If set, ONLY paths matching one of these rules may be edited; everything else is denied (same rule grammar as deny).

hermes.customModes.markdownDescription: Custom modes restrict which files the agent may edit on the main edit path (`write_file`/`patch`). Rules: exact workspace-relative path (`src/app.ts`), directory prefix ending `/` (`src/`), or basename suffix (`*.env`). No globs/`**`/negation. A mode is a strong floor on the main edit path, **not a sandbox** — terminal, code execution, subagent, and MCP-tool writes bypass it; recovery for those is the post-turn checkpoint.

hermes.nextEdit.backend.description: Transport for Next Edit Suggestions (the NEXT source). Generic always uses the FIM model on `#hermes.autocomplete.endpoint#`, never this setting. Machine-scoped: a workspace cannot redirect where next-edit context is sent (security).

hermes.nextEdit.endpoint.markdownDescription: Base URL for the Next Edit Suggestions (NEXT) backend. Leave empty to use the backend's default. Generic always uses `#hermes.autocomplete.endpoint#` instead of this setting. Machine-scoped: a workspace cannot redirect where next-edit context is sent (security).

hermes.nextEdit.model.description: Model name/id used for Next Edit Suggestions (the NEXT source), e.g. a sweep-v2-7B GGUF import. Machine-scoped: a workspace cannot silently repoint next-edit requests at a different model (security).
